P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes. Under the FX framework of Law 14.286/2021, FX operations may be carried out freely with no value limit, under BCB regulation. Residents, individuals included, MAY KEEP abroad the foreign-currency proceeds of exports of goods and services (Law 11.371/2006 Art. 1 as rewritten by Law 14.286/2021). There is no obligation to bring money into Brazil or convert it. Residents with more than US$1 million in foreign assets at year end must file the BCB 'Capitais Brasileiros no Exterior' (CBE) declaration.

sources.quote: 1º Fica facultada a manutenção, no exterior, dos recursos em moeda estrangeira relativos aos recebimentos de exportações brasileiras de mercadorias e de serviços para o exterior, realizadas por pessoas físicas ou jurídicas residentes, domiciliadas ou com sede no País.

sources.title: Lei nº 14.286/2021 (novo marco cambial)

Resolução BCB 277/2022 (eFX limits, e.g. US$10,000 for certain transfers per a search summary) was not read. Income tax still applies to money kept abroad (L3).

P2_fcy_account.question: Can individuals hold a foreign-currency bank account?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Abroad: yes. Residents may keep export proceeds in financial institutions abroad (P1); foreign assets must be declared to the BCB above US$1m (CBE) and in the income tax return. Foreign-currency accounts INSIDE Brazil are left to BCB regulation (Law 14.286 gives the BCB power to regulate 'contas em moeda estrangeira no País'), and whether ordinary individuals may open one was NOT verified.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual selling digital products or services register a business? How (sole proprietor), cost, online?
L1_registration.answer: Not necessarily. Individuals can earn as a pessoa física (autônomo) and pay monthly carnê-leão on income from abroad (L3). The simplified business option is the MEI (Microempreendedor Individual): annual gross revenue up to R$81,000 (domestic and export combined), ONLY for occupations listed in Annex XI of CGSN Resolution 140/2018, at most one employee. It is exempt from IRPJ, CSLL, PIS/COFINS and IPI under SIMEI, and registered online via the Portal do Empreendedor (CNPJ). A bill (PLP 186/2026) proposing R$110k in 2027 is NOT in force.

L1_registration.notes: Whether typical digital freelancer occupations (programmer, designer, consultant) are in Annex XI was NOT checked; many intellectual professions are reportedly excluded. Otherwise options are Simples Nacional via an ME, or staying a pessoa física. Municipal registration for autônomos (ISS) was not researched.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax identification number requirement and how to get it
L2_tax_id.answer: CPF (Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas), the individual taxpayer number from Receita Federal. It is also the single national identification number on the new national ID card (CIN, Decree 10.977/2022) and is required by payment providers (Mercado Pago, Stripe). An MEI or company gets a CNPJ.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: How residents' foreign-sourced or digital income is taxed
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents who receive income from abroad (or from other individuals) must pay carnê-leão monthly. It is mandatory, and income from abroad is declared in the carnê-leão system. From January 2026 (Law 15.270/2025), monthly taxable income up to R$5,000 gets a tax reduction that brings the tax to zero, with a decreasing reduction between R$5,000.01 and R$7,350. Foreign tax paid can be credited where a treaty or reciprocity exists (search summary).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported services and digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: There's no single national VAT on services yet. Services pay municipal ISS (minimum 2%, maximum 5%, LC 116/2003). ISS does NOT apply to exports of services. BUT services developed in Brazil whose RESULT occurs in Brazil are not exports, even if the payer is abroad. MEIs pay ISS within the fixed monthly SIMEI amount (not extracted). The 2026-2033 consumption-tax reform (CBS/IBS) was not researched.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law: name, year, in force?, regulator
L5_data_protection.answer: LGPD, the Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados Pessoais (Law 13.709/2018, as amended by Law 13.853/2019), supervised by the Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD). Fines go up to 2% of the company's or group's revenue in Brazil, capped at R$50 million per infraction.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: E-commerce / consumer-protection law relevant to online sales
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Consumer Defence Code (Law 8.078/1990) Art. 49: consumers may withdraw within 7 days of signing or receiving the product or service when the purchase happens outside the business premises, which covers online. Decree 7.962/2013 (e-commerce): sellers' websites must prominently show the business name and CPF/CNPJ registration number, physical and electronic address, a contract summary before purchase, and clear means to exercise the withdrawal right, including through the same tool used to buy.

D1_id_document.answer: The Carteira de Identidade Nacional (CIN), the new national ID card under Federal Decree 10.977/2022. It uses the CPF as the single national identification number and replaces the old RG, which remains valid until 2032. A CPF is mandatory to apply.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: none of the major platform barriers apply. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Fully localized'). (6) Stripe accepts merchants here, so you can take card payments directly on your own site. (7) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
